explanation: Read buildings east to west and keep a stack of candidates with strictly decreasing heights. A new building removes every earlier candidate no taller than it. Reverse the surviving indices to report west to east.
timeComplexity: O(n): each building is pushed once and popped at most once, then each survivor is emitted once. Reverse scans visit each building once; stack scans push/pop each building at most once.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary candidate-stack storage in the worst case, plus O(v) returned indices; the stack can peak above final output size. Reverse scans retain a running maximum; forward scans additionally retain candidate buildings.

correctness: Every removed building has a newer, western building at least as tall, so cannot see the sunset. Surviving candidates remain strictly decreasing in east-to-west order. Any later blocker would remove its blocked predecessor, so all and only final survivors are visible; reversing gives the required order.
walkthrough: For [5,9,4,7,3], push index 0, then index 1 removes 0. Push 2; index 3 removes 2. Push 4. The surviving stack indices are [1,3,4], so return [4,3,1].
edgeCases: Equal-height western buildings block earlier buildings because the comparison is strict.
The westernmost building is visible, even if its height equals int.MinValue.
